briefing:
إليك التقرير التكتيكي الشامل للجولة السادسة، المعد خصيصاً لقيادة فريقك نحو قفزة نوعية في الترتيب العام باستخدام التحليل الرياضي المتقدم ومحرك القواعد الذهبية التاريخية.

---

### 1. التكتيك المعتمد وموقف الترتيب: الاستهداف الهجومي التعويضي (AGGRESSIVE)
في مركزنا الحالي (10,600,116)، يصبح اللعب السلبي أو تتبع "التمبلت" السائد بمثابة تراجع مستمر. الاستراتيجية المعتمدة لهذه الجولة هي **الهجوم التعويضي الجريء (AGGRESSIVE)**. نمتلك قوة مالية كامنة في البنك تبلغ **£2.8m**، وهي ميزة تكتيكية هائلة تمنحنا مرونة الحركة السريعة. التحول إلى تشكيل (3-5-2) يمنحنا الكثافة الهجومية المطلوبة في خط الوسط مع الحفاظ على هيكل دفاعي متوازن. أخذ سالب (-4) في هذه المرحلة ليس تراجعاً، بل هو استثمار مدروس بعناية لتحقيق قفزة نوعية تفوق تكلفة التبديل، مستهدفين تقليص الفارق مع المنافسين عبر أصول ذات ملكية منخفضة وسقف نقاط مرتفع (High-Upside Differentials).

### 2. مدى مطابقة القرارات للقواعد الذهبية (Gold Rules Compliance)
تخضع قراراتنا التكتيكية لهذه الجولة لغربلة صارمة عبر محرك القواعد الذهبية التاريخية، وتأتي المطابقة على النحو التالي:
*   **جدوى السالب (-4 Hit):** تشير القاعدة الذهبية إلى أن أخذ "السالب" كان تاريخياً مثالياً لالتقاط الانفجارات الرقمية للاعبين (بنسبة ثقة 80%). تبديلاتنا تحقق زيادة فورية صافية متوقعة تبلغ **+4.03 نقطة** بعد خصم السالب، مما يشرعن القرار رياضياً.
*   **توزيع ميزانية خط الوسط:** تفرض القاعدة الذهبية تركيز الميزانية في خط الوسط (بنسبة 39.8% من الإنفاق الأساسي). بوجود ساكا، بالمر، برونو فيرنانديز، تافيرنييه، والوافد الجديد كامادا، نحن نمتلك خط وسط فتاكاً يطابق تماماً هذا النمط التاريخي الناجح.
*   **كفاءة الأسعار (Price Efficiency):** تؤكد القاعدة أن اللاعبين الأقل من £6.0m يقدمون أعلى معدل نقاط لكل مليون (2.69 pts/£m). انتداب إيمرسون (£5.5m) وكامادا (£5.0m) يجسد هذه القاعدة حرفياً، حيث نشتري نقاطاً متوقعة عالية بأقل تكلفة ممكنة.
*   **شارة القيادة الاقتصادية:** تشير القاعدة الذهبية إلى أن كباتن النخبة تاريخياً بلغ متوسط سعرهم £6.5m (مع كبتنة اللاعبين الـ Premium بنسبة 20% فقط). اختيارنا لكابتن متوسط السعر يتماشى تماماً مع هذه الإحصائية التاريخية الصادمة التي تتفوق على الخيارات البديهية.

### 3. التحليل الرياضي والتكتيكي للتبديلات (3-GW Horizon)
*   **🔴 بيع Akpom (xP: 1.7) ──► 🟢 شراء Emersonn (xP: 6.8 | £5.5m):**
    تخلصنا من أصل شبه ميت هجومياً لصالح إيمرسون (IPS) الذي يمتلك معدل نقاط متوقعة مرتفع جداً (6.8) لهذه الجولة. يواجه فولهام على أرضه (FDR: 2)، وهي مباراة مثالية للانفجار الهجومي. على مدار الجولات الثلاث القادمة [FUL (H), MCI (A), NFO (H)]، يمثل إيمرسون ترقية هائلة تضمن لنا المشاركة الأساسية والتهديد الهجومي المستمر.
*   **🔴 بيع Gakpo (xP: 0.0) ──► 🟢 شراء Kamada (xP: 5.3 | £5.0m):**
    إصابة جاكبو في الكاحل وغيابه غير المحدد جعل بيعه حتمياً بلا عواطف. البديل كامادا (CRY) يدخل التشكيلة بـ xP يبلغ 5.3 ومباراة ممتازة على أرضه ضد نوتنغهام فورست (FDR: 3). جدول كريستال بالاس القادم [NFO (H), BHA (A), NEW (H)] يمنح كامادا فرصة ذهبية لتقديم عوائد هجومية مستمرة، مستفيداً من سعره الاقتصادي (£5.0m) الذي يحرر لنا الميزانية.
*   **الحسبة الرياضية الصافية:** مجموع النقاط المتوقعة للاعبين المغادرين هو (1.7)، بينما مجموع القادمين هو (12.1). الفارق الإيجابي الضخم (+10.4) يغطي تكلفة السالب (-4) باريحية تامة ويحقق عائداً فورياً ومستقبلياً مضموناً.

### 4. مبررات شارة القيادة (C) والنائب (VC)
*   **الكابتن (C): João Pedro (CHE) - xP: 7.8**
    تم تسليم شارة القيادة لـ جواو بيدرو بناءً على تفوقه المطلق في نموذج النقاط المتوقعة (7.8 xP). يتوافق هذا القرار مع القاعدة الذهبية التي تفضل الكباتن ذوي الأسعار المتوسطة لتعظيم العائد على الاستثمار. تشيلسي يمر بفترة هجومية قوية، وبيدرو يمتلك السقف الأعلى (Explosive Upside) في هذه الجولة لضرب دفاعات الخصم.
*   **النائب (VC): Emersonn (IPS) - xP: 6.8**
    تم اختيار إيمرسون كأصل احتياطي استراتيجي للقيادة. يلعب على أرضه (Home Fixture) ضد فولهام، وهو ما يطابق قاعدة الكابتن التي تشير إلى أن 40% من الكباتن التاريخيين لعبوا على أرضهم مع FDR سهل (<= 2). في حال حدوث أي غياب مفاجئ لبيدرو، فإن إيمرسون جاهز تماماً لتحمل المسؤولية.

### 5. استراتيجية الخواص وحماية ميزانية الفريق
التوصية الفنية حاسمة: **الاحتفاظ بجميع الخواص المتاحة (Wildcard, Free Hit, Triple Captain, Bench Boost)**. تفعيل أي خاصية في هذه الجولة العادية يعتبر هدراً تكتيكياً؛ القيمة الرياضية القصوى لهذه الخواص تتضاعف فقط في جولات الدبل (Double Gameweeks) حيث يمكننا تحقيق عوائد تفوق 150+ نقطة. 
في الوقت ذاته، قمنا بحماية ميزانيتنا بذكاء عبر الإبقاء على **£2.8m** كسيولة نقدية في البنك، مما يتيح لنا اقتناص أي لاعب متفجر في الجولات القادمة دون الحاجة لخصم نقاط إضافي. كما قمنا بتطهير الفريق من المخاطر العالية بوضع إيزاك (المصاب) وسوبوسلاي وكونسا على رادار البيع الفوري لتجنب هبوط الأسعار وخسارة القيمة السوقية.

---

### الخلاصة التنفيذية
لقد تم تصميم هذه الجولة بمشرط جراحي رقمي؛ تخلصنا من الأصول المصابة وغير المنتجة (جاكبو وأكبوم)، واستبدلناهما بقوة هجومية صاعدة (إيمرسون وكامادا) تحقق عائداً فورياً يتجاوز قيمة السالب المتخذ. قيادة "جواو بيدرو" هي مغامرة محسوبة تدعمها الأرقام والتاريخ. نحن ندخل الجولة السادسة بتشكيل (3-5-2) مرن، وسيولة مالية ضخمة في البنك، وترسانة كاملة من الخواص غير الملموسة، مستعدين تماماً لبدء رحلة الصعود العمودي في الترتيب العام.

Cottage Tactico: High intensity Tractor Boys
press_wire.summary: As Fulham return to action for a run of fixtures against the three newly promoted sides, in Ipswich Town they first face the most familiar of the three. That is not just because Ipswich have been in the Premier League more recently than Hull and Coventry. They firstly, quite literally have a pair of familiar faces in Saša Lukić and Issa Diop offering bite and experience that we know to be key when establishing yourself in the most brutally competitive top flight in the world. They also have Gary O’Neil, a manager with some established tendencies in this league and who seems to have embraced at least one core dynamic from their previous stint under Kieran McKenna. So here’s what Fulham need to be aware of as we go in search of our first win of the season at Portman Road on Saturday afternoon. SAME, SAME, BUT DIFFERENT Like any Tactico, I hopped onto the Kieran McKenna hype train during Ipswich’s back-to-back promotion era. And despite being under new management for their latest Premier League campaign there is some continuity in their setup and approach this time around. McKenna set up Ipswich in a 4-2-3-1 with a couple of very notable features. Firstly, it was a 4-2-3-1 which genuinely had that structure in the middle of the park. So many setups, including Fulham’s own for multiple years under Marco Silva, flit between a 4-3-3 and 4-2-3-1 with many elements of a single pivot and two 8s on display even if on paper there appears to be a double pivot and a clear roaming number 10. That is not really the case for Ipswich, who historically had the likes of Sam Morsy and Massimo Luongo providing a combative base allowing their No 10, Conor Chaplin, to focus on final third impact. They’ve now replicated that approach with Lukić and Exequiel Palacios in the two and Julio Enciso [more on him later] unleashed to attack ahead of them. The second bit of continuity is the player whose role has stood out more than any other over this era of Ipswich’s renaissance. Leif Davis might be a LB, but he has also been the creative centrepiece of this Ipswich side for 5 seasons now. Davis (3) bombs on to such an extent that his average positions often look something like a winger. Not only that but he possesses the technical quality to make something happen when he gets into those high positions. From LB, Davis put up 37 goal + assist involvements across those League 1 and Championship promotion runs under McKenna in 22/23 and 23/24. His two goals and one assist in five Premier League games so far this season already matches his tally from the last time Town were in the top flight, suggesting he might do better at translating that final third impact across this time around. O’Neil has so far had two different wing options ahead of Davis. Daizen Maeda perhaps offers more direct off the ball running, while Jack Clarke has more craft on the ball. But both enjoy cutting inside and offer 2v2 combo threats down this flank. For all the danger that might spell for Fulham, every strength also delivers opportunity. Space behind the roaming Davis can be found with Ipswich’s LCB tasked with trying to cover it should opponents turn the ball over and attack swiftly. That hasn’t always looked straightforward for the likes of Jacob Greaves. Last time out in the Premier League, Davis occasionally took on the role of LWB in a five at the back with three CBs cutting down this channel space. Initially with the arrival of O’Neil - who has his own history of switching into five at the back with Wolves - many assumed this might be Ipswich’s direction of travel. It hasn’t been, formally at least, prior to the international break. PREMIER LEAGUE PHYSICALITY A regular theme in this preview series so far is the continued trend towards athleticism in the Premier League. Far from being the land of pure possession and patterns, our top flight has increasingly become one dominated by out of possession intensity and duel winning. This seems to be a lesson learnt by Ipswich who find themselves in a position familiar to Fulham fans - looking to establish themselves as a Premier League outlet having been promoted and relegated in successive seasons. You can see this in their recruitment. We are well accustomed to the physicality offered by Lukic and Diop. But similarly the energy and aggressiveness of Lukic’s partner in the middle of the park, Palacios, fits this mantra perfectly. Their tenacity shielding the defence should in theory protect the CBs from having to cover too much ground. Diop’s dominance in the box has added to the likes of Greaves and Dara O’Shea who have plenty of aerial ability when needed. But far from being a side that just passively sits, there is a bit of ‘all action’ in this Ipswich side. This can be seen clearly in their running numbers. Only Brentford and Bournemouth have covered more distance sprinting so far this season than Ipswich, who also (like Fulham) rank highly for high intensity distance covered. We should expect to come up against a side ready to battle and adept at recovery runs, as well as attacking at speed going the other way too. The comfort with high intensity counterattacks will be unsurprising for those familiar with O’Neil’s work at Wolves where the likes of Matheus Cunha and Pedro Neto looked pretty lethal on the break. Opponents need to be wary of this dynamic continuing with some dynamic forwards at Ipswich still bedding into the side. IT’S NOT GOING TO BE DULL (SURELY?) That end to end tendency in Ipswich’s games is perhaps in keeping with some of what we’ve grown accustomed to in SW6 this season. Ipswich are one of only three teams to have faced more shots on their goal than Fulham and their xG against like ours is one of the highest in the league. And on the measure that really counts, only Chelsea’s 12 goals conceded exceeds Ipswich’s 11. So there are reasons to be optimistic that Fulham might have some chances to score on Saturday afternoon. However, Ipswich offer plenty to fear themselves. While their goals scored, shots taken and xG created are largely middle of the road the quality of the shots they do create really stands out. Only Man City have created higher quality chances on average than Ipswich and a look at their Premier League goal catalogue this season shows a number of crosses and cutbacks generating chances close to goal for strikers like Emersonn and Zian Flemming who have real box presence. The energy and exuberance of their midfield often acts as a catalyst for their attacks. With hard running on and off the ball helping Ipswich create chances against stretched or unsettled defences, be that on the counter attack when sat off deeper or after winning the ball higher in the press. Because these transition moments allow attacks when defences are not organised as they’d ideally want to be in settled possession the chances generated tend to be more clear cut. THE KEY - JULIO ENCISO If you’re playing 4-2-3-1, your ideal No 10 needs to provide reliable goal involvements and be comfortable leading your press out of possession. As a newly promoted side, finding someone who can do one of these things to a top level in the Premier League is hard enough. To find one that does both is massive. Early signs are that with Enciso, Ipswich Town might have nailed it. Only Bruno Fernandes and Cunha have received more line breaking receptions this season than Enciso. And when watching him it is striking how often he receives in a way that opens him up to drive forward energetically with balance that lets him go in either direction. Enciso’s 3 goal contributions also show that these receptions often lead to end product. That is perhaps unsurprising given his clear technical gifts. But beyond that I’ve been impressed by his engine for a player primarily lauded for technical and creative ability. Enciso has shown he can be a nuisance off the ball and use that work rate to create turnover opportunities that let him burst into space on the counterattack. For the Fulham defence, it seems obvious that the less we see of him on Saturday, the better this one is likely to go. TEAM NEWS | DUO RULED OUT OF PALACE TRIP
press_wire.summary: Boss reveals latest team news Duo ruled out of Palace clash Williams a doubt for match Oliver Glasner confirmed Nikola Milenković and Igor Jesus will both miss Nottingham Forest’s Premier League trip to Crystal Palace. The duo, who remained at the Nigel Doughty Academy during the international break, have both picked up knocks which mean they will be unavailable for the game. The boss says Jesus is likely to be out of action for a few weeks, while Neco Williams is also a doubt through illness. A number of Forest players featured regularly for their nations over the break, but Glasner emphasised that this is something all Premier League coaches have to contend with during these spells. “We have two injured players who were here and not away on international duty. The internationals came back well and fit. “Nikola Milenković, he returned from an injury and played in the friendly, which was all good, but he injured his knee in a duel and he has a bruised bone. “He will miss the game; it’s very painful, so he can’t train. “The other is Igor Jesus. He has a muscle injury in his calf and he will be out for a few weeks. That’s not what we wanted. The other who is questionable is Neco Williams. “He returned well and trained with us yesterday, but he didn’t feel well. He had a fever in the night and was not available today, but we will see how he recovers tomorrow. “It’s been an intense period for the international players, but this is the same for every Premier League team. You just have to deal with it.”
